clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad: PoolManager-only replay of mined transactions in the reference interpreter, 3,507 transactions from blocks 124691690 to 124991689; 3507 of 3507 match in frames, logs and storage.
clearedSpotChecks.note: raw/pm-143all.jsonl has 3,507 rows, all with matching frames, logs and diffMode storage, and 2,446 with a matching eth_getStorageAt comparison, as stated. Three random rows checked with eth_getTransactionReceipt at https://rpc.monad.xyz (an endpoint the replay did not use for receipts) give the recorded block, status 1 and the recorded PoolManager log counts (2, 1, 3). I reran pmreplay.py on 0x0786577accca5be6bfc11ee89a214646cd6ac7be7c9b6769ce27081e736de47d (block 124724071, beforeSwap hook that returned a nonzero delta, last PoolManager transaction of its block): 8 frames, 2 of 2 logs, 2 of 2 storage words against diffMode and against eth_getStorageAt, all matched. The method has a limit. Outgoing calls are answered from the recorded call tree, so only the PoolManager's own code is tested, and only on inputs that were mined. The research states this limit and files the unmined branches as a lead.

clearedSpotChecks.check: MegaETH: whole history replayed (1,567 transactions); 1566 match, one set aside as the PoolManager's own CREATE2 deployment.
clearedSpotChecks.note: raw/pm-4326.jsonl gives 1,566 matched rows and one unmatched row, 0x5dcf1f70a22336034026a649957a4b8b1370f5c6d8731f19ca99605db595a301. eth_getTransactionByHash at https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc shows it is a call to the deterministic deployer 0x4e59b44847b379578588920ca78fbf26c0b4956c with 48,518 bytes of input. Its only log is OwnershipTransferred (topic 0x8be0079c) from the PoolManager, and its single storage difference is slot 0 set to the owner, so setting it aside is correct. Four random receipts match the recorded log counts. Rerunning 0x2f5b7e04ea5a4dbffb8f7e55f0769ee713fc22c04069202ef814621ab82648c7 matched in 11 frames and 1 log, with no storage written. The call frames compared on MegaETH come from a revm re-execution, so a frame-level fault in the sequencer that leaves logs and storage unchanged would not be seen. The research says this.

clearedSpotChecks.check: HyperEVM: whole history replayed (2,763 transactions); 2762 match, one set aside as the deployment. Storage compared against public replay clients, not the validator.
clearedSpotChecks.note: raw/pm-999.jsonl gives 2,762 matched rows and the unmatched row 0x886b45bc662d93a4b74935513eb8dc8c1179c4a6c70056f4b4ba5b251c58e4c5. At https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm that transaction is a deployer call whose only log is OwnershipTransferred. Four random receipts from the validator endpoint match the recorded PoolManager log counts. Rerunning 0x0239278234195833c7a8bbf389b32e6726bd568f4fed33fc14bb1daa758ba964 (block 49863033) matched in 10 frames, 3 logs and 2 storage words against diffMode and against the block. eth_getCode at all three endpoints in networks.json returns 24,009 bytes. Against build/PoolManager.json these differ only at bytes 13618 to 13637, which hold each deployment's own address inside the immutable reference that starts at 13606. That supports the claim that the code is the same byte for byte. HyperEVM storage is compared with a replay client, not with validator state, as the research states, so this link rests on the receipts the validator produced.
